title: sampling-and-backpressure-midweek-cribsheet-2026-10-14
content:
Midweek cribsheet from the serving-runtime sync (focus: sampling thresholds and backpressure behavior for KV-shadow/prefill pipeline). Quick, messy notes intended for iteration, not final design.

Attendees: Aisha (notes), Diego, Rina, Evan, Priya, Sam (brief), ops on standby.

Agenda:
- Quick status on current sampling experiment (SERV-1427)
- Backpressure symptoms observed during 10/12 spike
- Proposed heuristics for dynamic sampling + circuit-breaker thresholds
- Rollout plan + what to monitor

Summary of current state:
- Experiment SERV-1427 (adaptive prefill sampling) has been running on canary for 48h.
  - Canary config: sample_prob=0.35 -> 0.55 depending on qps per-shard; prefill window 256 tokens.
  - Observed: 12% drop in average GPU token cost when sample_prob > 0.45, but p95 latency increases by ~6% on long-context (>1024) requests.
  - Memory: KV-shadow hit-rate improved marginally (from 62% -> 68%).

Backpressure incident on 2026-10-12 (post-deploy):
- Trigger: correlated burst from Partner-A caused queue growth on kernel-worker-group-7.
- Symptom: coalescer attempted to batch >16 requests with heterogeneous sequence lengths; prefill worker blocked waiting on KV fetch and timed out, causing partial fallbacks to small-batch path.
- Mitigation applied: manual scale-up of kernel-worker-group-7 and temporarily disabled aggressive sampling on canary.
- Follow-up: need automated graceful degradation that avoids p95 regressions while preserving cost wins.

Discussion notes / ideas captured:
1) Two-tier sampling with warm-start biasing
   - Idea: split sample decision into fast-path (edge) and slow-path (controller). Fast-path sampling uses simple heuristics (recent kv-hit, request-size) to decide on immediate skipping of prefill. Controller adjusts global sample_prob periodically based on per-shard pressure signals.
   - Expected: avoids heavy controller roundtrips but still reacts to cluster pressure.
2) Backpressure-aware batch sizing
   - Heuristic: cap micro-batches by percentile of recent sequence-length distribution; if micro-batch contains > X% long sequences, prefer smaller batches or route to fast-fallback model.
   - Concrete numbers debated: X = 30% looked reasonable in lab runs.
3) Soft-circuit for prefill RFC
   - When kv-fetch tail latency > 95th threshold for 30s, start incrementally reducing prefill sampling and increase fallback probability. Revert when tail improves.
4) Prefill shadow-sampling to reduce regressions
   - Always run a tiny shadow prefill for a sample of requests to surface quality regressions from higher sampling without incurring full cost.

Decisions made (tentative):
- Implement a backpressure signal (BPS) exported by kernel workers: two values (queue-depth-estimate, kv-fetch-95ms) aggregated per-shard and published every 10s. Owner: Diego. Due: 2026-10-20. (JIRA: SERV-1379)
- Add edge-fast-path sampler that uses request metadata (recent_kv_hit boolean, seq_len bucket, client-tier) to make a cheap binary sampling decision. Owner: Rina. Due: 2026-10-22.
- Prototype micro-batch pctl cap (start with p75 cap) in coalescer; fallback routing to small-batch path when cap exceeded. Owner: Evan. Due: 2026-10-21.

Action items (short):
- Diego: emit BPS metrics and a small ingestion job that aggregates per-shard signals. (SERV-1379) Due 2026-10-20.
- Rina: PR for edge sampler binary using request headers + local cache of recent_kv_hit. Link PR -> GH/678 for pattern. Due 2026-10-22.
- Evan: add configurable pctl cap to coalescer and exercise in unit tests + canary. Add a switch to route long-seq batches to fallback. Due 2026-10-21.
- Priya: update SLO playbook to include temporary rollback steps and monitoring queries (grafana panels) to watch p95/p99 latency and token-cost delta. Due 2026-10-19.
- Aisha: run a short quality regression harness against shadow-prefill window; capture differences in top-1 completion for 5k prompt set. Due 2026-10-18.

Tests & metrics to capture during rollout:
- Kernel-level: avg batch size, batch variance, kernel-utilization (GPU %), queue-depth-estimate, kv-fetch-95
- App-level: p50/p95/p99 generation latency, token-cost per request, percent of fallback-route activations
- Quality: top-1 parity vs baseline on preselected prompt set (sample of 5k).

Open questions / risks:
- Quality risk: shadow-prefill needs to be large enough to detect subtle regressions; how to pick sample size vs cost budget? (Priya to advise)
- Oscillation risk: controller adjusting sample_prob too aggressively could cause thrashing; we should add dampening (exponential backoff on change rate).
- Observability gaps: we currently do not export per-request tag that indicates a prefill decision origin (edge vs controller); add a small log field.

Rollout plan (sketch):
1) Implement metrics + edge sampler + coalescer cap behind feature flags (2 weeks): owners above.
2) Canary deploy to 5% traffic for 48h with shadow-prefill enabled for 1% of canary traffic. Monitor metrics above.
3) Gradual increase to 25% if no p95 regressions >5% and token-cost improvement sustained.
4) Full rollout only after two successful 25% waves and sign-off from SRE + Product.

Backlog / Nice-to-have items:
- ML model to predict prefill benefit per-request (longer term)
- Client SDK hints so partners can give preferred sampling preference for certain workloads
- Offline simulator to replay production traffic and model sampling/backpressure tradeoffs

Notes to self / TODOs for next sync:
- Capture a runbook snippet for operator-triggered temp-disable of controller adjustments. (Aisha)
- Rina to post initial edge-sampler PR for review and call out expected perf microbench numbers.
- Evan to wire synthetic long-seq load test into nightly pipelines.

Raw telemetry snapshot from canary (10/14 06:00-12:00 UTC):
- Avg batch size: 7.3 -> 6.1 during 10/12 spike
- Kernel-utilization: 54% steady, peaked 92% at 10/12 03:11 UTC
- KV-fetch-95: baseline 48ms -> spike 620ms during incident
- Prefill shadow hit-rate (sampled): 69%

If you want to push any of these items to the main PR, add a comment in GH/678 or ping in #serving-runtime. This doc is raw; I'll tidy into a proper RFC if we converge on heuristics next week.
